result.title: Patch-Derived or Register Tokens? Comparing Variable-Length Image Tokenizers
result.summary: Image tokenizers convert pixels into compact latent sequences for efficient generative modeling. Most approaches arrange latents on a downsampled two-dimensional grid, tying sequence length to image resolution. We compare two variable-length strategies: computationally efficient patch-derived tokens, which inherit explicit spatial organization, and more demanding register tokens, which have no predefined spatial layout. Our reconstruction results reveal that patch-derived tokens perform substantially better under extreme compression, whereas register tokens achieve slightly better reconstruction quality at intermediate budgets. At high token budgets, both approaches achieve similar reconstruction quality. For downstream generative tasks, register tokens outperform patch-derived tokens. Adding representation alignment with external pretrained visual encoders substantially improves the generative performance of patch-derived tokens, allowing them to match or outperform register tokens depending on the token budget. We further find that both approaches learn spatially localized representations. Patch-derived tokens largely retain their explicitly imposed spatial organization, while register tokens develop an implicit two-dimensional spatial structure despite having no predefined layout. Representation alignment reduces this spatial organizational constraint, enabling individual tokens to exert a stronger non-local influence.

AI.brief_summary: 比较两种可变长度图像 tokenizer 策略：继承显式空间结构的 patch-derived tokens 与无预定义布局、计算开销更大的 register tokens，考察二者在不同 token 预算下的重建与下游生成表现，并检验与外部预训练视觉编码器做表示对齐的效果。
AI.relevance_reason: 可变长度视觉 token、表示对齐与 token 空间局部性/非局部影响的分析，可能为 LVR 中视觉细节在压缩下的保留、token 预算与长度变化时的证据筛选提供方法线索；但论文面向图像生成，未涉及推理期 latent 状态，联系需核查。
